name: EDM/hardstyle spectral tilt reference
what_this_is: A pink-noise-referenced spectral tilt, not a measured hardstyle band table.
The target band profile is computed from the tilt at run time (see
target_profile() in master.py), so the whole curve is one documented number

provenance.basis: Published EDM mastering guidance: a ~1.5 dB/octave downward tilt is the commonly cited starting balance for EDM, with the caveat that the best value varies by track and subgenre.
provenance.not_sourced_from: No public, numeric, hardstyle-specific target spectrum was found. Commercial genre curves (e.g. iZotope Tonal Balance Control) exist but their values are proprietary and are not reproduced here.

limits: A genre tilt describes what EDM masters typically do on average. It does not
describe what this set should do, and matching it does not make a mix sound

better_option: Once a mix has been listened to and approved, measure it and use it as the reference instead: `--eq match --reference <that>.wav`. A reference someone chose with their ears beats a genre average.
